headline: Taiwan’s Vessel Map Puts Sustained Coercion to the Test
deck: A map identified Chinese warships and other official vessels, including the Liaoning east of the Philippines; subsequent deployments will test whether pressure is sustained.
body: Reuters reported that Taiwan released a map of Chinese naval and other official vessels, including the carrier Liaoning’s group east of the Philippines. An Asia Daily account of the map identified 34 navy warships and 19 Coast Guard and other official vessels. [E1][E2][E3][E10]

Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense reported six PLA aircraft sorties, seven PLAN ships and one other official ship around Taiwan as of 6 a.m. local time; five aircraft sorties entered its northern, central and southwestern air-defense identification zone. [E4][E5]

The response follows a visible chain: Taiwan’s armed forces said they monitored detected activity and then used combat air patrol aircraft, navy ships and coastal missile systems. Continued activity can therefore require a continuing response across those forces, rather than a count that ends with a single report. [E6]

Earlier this month, Taiwan’s defense ministry said it was closely watching for large-scale Chinese exercises during the traditional peak season for PLA drills and was using joint intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities to follow the PLA. [E7][E8]
The paper last covered Chinese live-fire boxes near Dongshan in July. [E11]

**The desk's reading.** The published count makes sustained regional pressure a plausible concern because it places a carrier group east of the Philippines alongside Taiwan’s reported activity around the island. The strongest competing reading is Beijing’s: the PLA Navy has said its drills were "not directed at any country or target," and the available record does not establish a coordinated combat rehearsal. [E9]

**The next test.** Over the next 72 hours, sustained coercion would show in renewed or expanded Chinese deployments and an official Taiwanese, Japanese or Philippine response that treats them as linked; a return to isolated movements without such a response would support the routine-training account.
